Alex — great to speak. See a concise recap below with a worked example based on the 150M–350M token band you quoted. I included recommended next steps at the bottom so procurement/engineering have a clear path.

Quick summary of private deployment licensing options
- VPC (hosted private control plane): monthly subscription + per-token slabs. Subscription covers control plane, monitoring, and base support.
- On-prem (air-gapped / customer-managed): one-time platform license + annual maintenance fee + per-token runtime usage slabs.

Support tiers (examples)
- Standard: business hours support, ticket SLA 8 hours, best-effort on-call.
- Premium: 24x7 escalation, 2-hour incident response, quarterly review.
- Enterprise: dedicated technical account manager, 1-hour incident response, custom SLA and compliance package.

Environment pricing note
- Each environment (prod/staging/DR/sandbox) can be licensed independently or bundled. Typical POC setups bundle staging+sandbox. A three-environment footprint (prod + staging + sandbox) is common. DR is priced as an add-on or part of Enterprise.

Worked example (illustrative, pre-negotiation)
Assumptions: model footprint optimized with quantization and prefix caching; effective tokens served = billed tokens.
- 150M tokens/month: VPC estimated unit rate range: $700/$1M (high) — $520/$1M (low with 12-mo commit).
- 250M tokens/month: VPC typical: $620/$1M; with environment bundle (3 envs) and Premium support, target $580/$1M.
- 350M tokens/month: VPC with 12-mo commit + operational optimizations: $480–$540/$1M.

On-prem notes (higher up-front; lower marginal token cost as commitment grows)
- One-time license: example $120k–$250k (depending on env count & cluster size) + annual maintenance 12–18% of license.
- Per-token slab after license: effective $/1M tokens often 10–35% below comparable VPC rates at volumes >300M/month due to amortization.

Next steps we recommend
1) Quick econ sketch from our side for the three volume scenarios (I will attach a spreadsheet).
2) Technical follow-up to size environments (prod/staging/sandbox + optional DR).
3) Procurement: preliminary license sketch & sample SOW for Nexia to review.
4) Security: we'll send the SOC2 evidence pack and a short checklist for on-prem network requirements.

Attached: nexia_econ_workup.xlsx (price bands + example calc), redwood_license_sketch_v1.pdf (sample SOW + license options)

I’ll loop Karthik and Marissa to lock down the conservative/optimistic unit rates for negotiation. Let me know if procurement wants a tighter anchor — we can propose a committed discount if Nexia prefers a 12-month minimum.

Best,
